Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed argument deterministically selects the awaited branch, the prior argument deterministically selected the immediate-render branch, and the transitive refresh boundaries and 2-second cold readiness bound are explicit in repository code. Actual delay varies with cache/session warmth, which affects severity rather than mechanism confidence.
Findings.PerformanceResource: filesystem discovery and agent-host session-state/IPC waits performed by the migration refresh
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The delay grows with cold prompt-file discovery and agent-host readiness; the remote source-folder provider can wait up to its 2-second first-snapshot timeout, while additional enabled categories add parallel discovery/provider work whose slowest operation gates navigation.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: blocked migration-page navigation and increased perceived latency after clicking any affected setting's deprecation link
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The link passed `migrationCategory: ConfiguredLocations`; `startCustomizationMigration(categoryId)` entered and rendered that category immediately, allowing the existing loading state to appear while the editor's background refresh completed.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The link now omits `migrationCategory`, so `startCustomizationMigration()` follows the overview branch, which awaits `refreshCustomizationMigrationInfo()` before calling `showCustomizationMigrationDashboard()`. That refresh computes every enabled category, lists prompt files, and queries source folders before the migration view is shown.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `arguments: [{ migration: true }]` at line 298 replaces the category-specific argument. This selects the no-category branch in `showCustomizationMigrationPage`, whose first operation is `await this.refreshCustomizationMigrationInfo()`, unlike the prior category branch that renders immediately.
Findings.Title: Show the migrations view before awaiting its refresh
Findings.Impact: On a cold agent-host session or uncached prompt discovery, clicking “Migrations tab” in any of the five deprecation messages can leave the user on the previous UI for up to the remote snapshot wait (plus discovery time) before the migrations page appears.
Findings.Evidence: `OpenEditor` awaits `pane.startCustomizationMigration(migrationCategory)`. With the changed undefined category, `showCustomizationMigrationPage` awaits the complete refresh before preparing the migration view. `computeCustomizationMigrationInfo` awaits all enabled `computeMigration` calls; those call `listPromptFiles`, and then `provideSourceFolders`. For the agent-host provider, `provideSourceFolders` awaits `whenCustomizationsReady`, which explicitly permits a cold first-snapshot wait up to 2000 ms. The editor already starts this refresh in the background, so the diff primarily moves that existing expensive work onto the click-to-page critical path rather than adding useful prerequisite work.
Findings.Recommendation: Enter the migration view and render its loading state before awaiting the refresh, then update the dashboard when the refresh settles; keep the desired generic dashboard destination without gating first paint on discovery.

Scenarios.Scenario: Click a custom-location setting deprecation link to open migrations
Scenarios.CriticalPath: `OpenEditor` awaits `startCustomizationMigration`. After this diff the undefined category branch awaits the full migration refresh before entering/rendering the dashboard; previously the configured-location category view rendered immediately and refresh remained background work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover prompt/customization files through `listPromptFiles` and prompt file locators.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical listing per enabled prompt type on a cold cache: prompt, agent, instructions, and skill are possible; duplicate requests across categories share the per-type cached promise once file-locator event caching is active.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same editor refresh performed discovery in the background, but the category-specific migration page rendered without awaiting it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: After the route change, the slowest enabled category's listings must settle before the dashboard is shown.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Wait for the agent-host session customization snapshot and derive writable source folders.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to one source-folder call per candidate target type within each enabled file category, plus one aggregate call per distinct target type; with all three file categories populated this can reach nine provider calls, though readiness shares one memoized snapshot wait.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These calls already occurred, but did not block the prior category deep link's first render.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The first cold call can wait for the session snapshot, explicitly bounded at 2000 ms, and now gates showing the dashboard.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Compute MCP migration through the active harness provider when that experimental category is enabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider computation per coalesced migration refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: It was part of the background all-category refresh and did not gate rendering the configured-location category page.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: It joins the `Promise.all` whose completion now gates dashboard navigation; exact provider boundary cost depends on the active harness.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Enabled migration categories, distinct prompt target types, cold discovered source folders/files, and readiness of the active agent-host session. Effective file listing cardinality is reduced by per-type promise caching.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Refresh requests are coalesced by a zero-delay `Delayer`; enabled categories run concurrently via `Promise.all`. File listings within each category use `Promise.all`, while source-folder target types in `createFileMigration` are queried serially. The aggregate target-folder pass is parallel. The diff does not increase concurrency, but makes completion of the aggregate refresh a navigation prerequisite.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm `listPromptFiles` calls return cached promises, and agent-host readiness is memoized per subscription. Cold caches perform file discovery and may wait up to 2 seconds for the first remote snapshot. The changed navigation remains blocked in both cases, with materially larger cost cold.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed command argument deterministically selects the only branch that awaits refresh before showing the migration UI.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Warm sessions may make the delay small, and MCP provider cost varies, but the cold 2-second readiness bound and filesystem work are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity latency regression because existing filesystem/provider work is newly moved onto the click-to-dashboard critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the Agent Customizations editor normally and refresh migration candidates after file or configuration changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The editor starts migration refreshes asynchronously from content creation, input setup, session changes, and customization events. Candidate collection completes before cached summaries and whichever page is visible are updated.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover prompt files for enabled migration categories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one cold listing per prompt type after cache coalescing; subsequent refreshes use cached values until locator invalidation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Configured-location migration was already included in `CUSTOMIZATION_MIGRATION_CATEGORIES`, so its enabled scans occurred before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background for normal editor first paint; results affect migration counts when ready.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Obtain agent-host source folders/session customization state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per enabled category/target type as above, with a shared memoized readiness wait.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Unchanged; homepage membership does not control `getEnabledMigrationCategories`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background for normal editor opening; can delay settled migration counts but not initial editor display.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of enabled categories, prompt types, candidates, and customization change events. Candidate summary filtering is linear in cached candidate count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Events call a zero-delay delayer and clear/cancel the prior request, preventing an unbounded queue. Enabled categories fan out concurrently; cancellation and sequence checks suppress stale completion.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Per-type file locations are cached and invalidated by locator/plugin changes. Failed/cancelled refreshes are not converted into success-shaped cache entries. The diff does not alter keys, invalidation, or lifetime.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that no new boundary is introduced in this scenario: scan selection comes from the unchanged full category registry.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Candidate collections can be large, but the added homepage membership only adds bounded extra passes over the configured-location candidate array; boundary behavior is unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding. The diff consumes already-computed configured-location candidates and does not increase scan frequency or boundary cardinality during ordinary refreshes.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render and interact with the migration dashboard after candidates have settled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Dashboard overview construction filters cached candidates by at most two scopes, then rebuilds dashboard DOM. Clicking the new configured-location row navigates to the existing category detail flow.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Configured-location candidate count C and scope count at most two. Overview filtering adds O(C) cached-object checks; rendered dashboard additions are bounded to one row per scope rather than one row per candidate.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous UI work only; no async boundary is initiated by adding the category to `homepageMigrationCategories`. Dashboard rebuilds remain serialized on the UI thread.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Uses `customizationsByMigrationCategory` populated by the prior refresh. No new cache or retained lifecycle is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High based on `getMigrationCandidates` being a map lookup plus optional array filter and `renderScope` rendering one row per non-empty category.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large candidate inventories increase filtering cost, but the work is simple and the DOM increase is constant, so there is no realistic independently reportable regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The added summary row and localization objects are bounded, and the detail UI already existed.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all six changed files. One introduced latency issue was reported: removing the category from the settings command route causes navigation to await the full migration refresh, moving cold filesystem and agent-host readiness work onto the first-render critical path. The new homepage category itself only summarizes cached candidates and adds bounded DOM work; no new scan, fan-out, cache-lifecycle, cleanup, retention, serialization, or concurrency regression was found.
